captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a customizable hobby knife handle consisting of three main parts shown in an exploded view. First, a long, slender cylindrical handle body with a hollow threaded end and debossed text running along its length. Second, a short sleeve with a textured knurled outer surface that slides onto the assembly. Third, a split-collet blade holder featuring a threaded shank on one end, a flared collar on the other, and a narrow central slit designed to clamp a hobby blade securely when tightened.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric 3D-printable hobby knife assembly in OpenSCAD. The design must include three separate, interlocking parts: a long cylindrical handle with internal threads and customizable text, a knurled sleeve, and a split-collet blade holder with a matching threaded shank and a blade slit.
captions.factory: The script uses three main modules: knife_handle(), knife_sleeve(), and knife_holder(). knife_handle() creates a main cylinder subtracted by a screw_thread() for internal threads and writecylinder() for text. knife_sleeve() uses a knurl() library function subtracted by internal clearance cylinders. knife_holder() combines a screw_thread() shank with a flared body created using cylinder() primitives, which is then split by subtracting a narrow cube() for the blade slit.
